results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. 

VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neuron information, parts, subclasses, and lineage clones. For example, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. However, for specific details about the subdivisions, the provided verbatim text from VFB is the relevant source.

results.question: What genetic tools are commonly used to label mushroom body neurons in Drosophila?

For more information on the genetic tools available for labeling Kenyon cell, you can explore the 92 records of transgene expression in Kenyon cell, or examine the expression patterns of specific constructs like PBac{602.P.SVS-1}Fas2[CPTI000483] and PBac{602.P.SVS-1}Sema1a[CPTI000505], which are listed in the VFBexp_FBti0144014 and VFBexp_FBti0144017 expression patterns, respectively. 

Additionally, VFB holds [32328](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") images of Kenyon cell, [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell, [79](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell") scRNAseq data records for Kenyon cell, [10073](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell, and [11243](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell, which may be useful for a narrower follow-up.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity, as recorded in VFB. It can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The giant fiber neuron enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge.

VFB holds various data related to the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") available images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") transgene expression reports in DNp01. The downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are numerous, with [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records, and the upstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are also extensive, with [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records. 

Relevant publications for the study of the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Power (1948), and many others, as cited in VFB. The connectivity of the giant fiber neuron can be explored further through the available data on its downstream and upstream connectivity classes.
